s1.tx: Before the beginning, before the mountains were raised, or ever the earth and the world were formed, there was God.
s1.pc: Bible-first anchor for the pre-temporal frame. The narration borrows the cadence of Psalm 90:2 to set the Father before the created order, asserting His priority over creation without describing a mechanism. D&C 93:29 confirms an eternal frame for both God and the intelligence of man.

b.text: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
b.comment: The narration echoes this verse's structure to place God prior to the created order.

r.text: Man was also in the beginning with God. Intelligence, or the light of truth, was not created or made, neither indeed can be.
r.comment: Confirms an eternal frame; offered as witness, not as premise.

s2.tx: And He, the Father of Spirits, conceived of our existence from before the foundation of the world, He knew us.
s2.pc: Container-word anchor. 'Father of spirits' (Hebrews 12:9) is a biblical title every tradition can receive; here it grounds the claim that our existence was His to conceive, joined to the foreknowledge of Ephesians 1:4 and Jeremiah 1:5.

b.text: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
b.comment: Supplies the biblical title carried by the span.

b.text: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:
b.comment: 'Before the foundation of the world' frame.

b.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee, and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations.
b.comment: Personal foreknowledge, here generalized to all.

r.text: Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones;
r.comment: Confirming witness to a premortal company of spirits.

s2b.tx: And so he moved to create us, to fellowship with Him and with one another.
s2b.pc: The purpose behind the creating: not existence only, but communion. The claim gathers from many witnesses rather than one—fellowship with Him (1 Corinthians 1:9; 1 John 1:3; the Lord walking in Eden) and fellowship with one another (Genesis 2:18; John 17; Zion's 'one heart and one mind'), the two great commandments of Matthew 22 binding the two together. Restoration scriptures add the creating's own stated purpose (Moses 1:39; 2 Nephi 2:25) and the communion's promised end (Revelation 21; Moses 7:64). Offered as a cumulative case, welcoming each tradition to fill it from its own scriptures.

b.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
b.comment: Made by divine counsel, in God's image—relational from the first word.

b.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
b.comment: The image, and 'male and female'—humanity made for relationship.

b.text: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.
b.comment: The Lord walking in the garden—the original communion creation was made for.

b.text: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
b.comment: Eternal life defined as knowing God—fellowship as the end itself.

b.text: God is faithful, by whom ye were called unto the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord.
b.comment: The explicit vertical purpose: called unto the fellowship of His Son.

b.text: That which we have seen and heard declare we unto you, that ye also may have fellowship with us: and truly our fellowship is with the Father, and with his Son Jesus Christ.
b.comment: Both directions in one verse: fellowship with the Father and Son, and with one another.

b.text: And I will set my tabernacle among you: and my soul shall not abhor you. And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and ye shall be my people.
b.comment: God's covenant aim: to dwell and walk among His people.

b.text: And let them make me a sanctuary; that I may dwell among them.
b.comment: The sanctuary built that God may dwell among them.

b.text: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
b.comment: Not made for isolation—'It is not good that the man should be alone.'

b.text: That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me.
b.comment: Union with one another patterned on the union of Father and Son.

b.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God … In whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit.
b.comment: No longer strangers, but one household built into a dwelling for God.

b.text: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
b.comment: The two loves that hold both directions together—God, and neighbor.

b.text: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
b.comment: The Shema—the Old Testament root of the first commandment.

b.text: Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the LORD.
b.comment: The Old Testament root of the second commandment.

b.text: And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.
b.comment: The communion consummated: the tabernacle of God with men.

b.text: And there shall be no more curse: but the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it; and his servants shall serve him: And they shall see his face; and his name shall be in their foreheads.
b.comment: The end of the story: His servants shall see His face.

r.text: For behold, this is my work and my glory—to bring to pass the immortality and eternal life of man.
r.comment: The creating's own stated purpose—God's work and glory in His children.

r.text: Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
r.comment: Creation ordered toward joy—men are, that they might have joy.

r.text: In the image of his own body, male and female, created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created and became living souls in the land upon the footstool of God.
r.comment: Made in the image of His own body, male and female—embodied relationship.

r.text: Verily, thus saith the Lord: It shall come to pass that every soul who forsaketh his sins and cometh unto me, and calleth on my name, and obeyeth my voice, and keepeth my commandments, shall see my face and know that I am;
r.comment: The promise of the vertical fellowship: to see His face and know Him.

r.text: And that same sociality which exists among us here will exist among us there, only it will be coupled with eternal glory, which glory we do not now enjoy.
r.comment: Fellowship is not left behind—the same sociality, coupled with glory.

r.text: And the Lord called his people Zion, because they were of one heart and one mind, and dwelt in righteousness; and there was no poor among them.
r.comment: Zion named for its fellowship: of one heart and one mind.

r.text: I say unto you, be one; and if ye are not one ye are not mine.
r.comment: The command that makes fellowship the mark of belonging: be one.

r.text: …are willing to bear one another’s burdens, that they may be light; Yea, and are willing to mourn with those that mourn; yea, and comfort those that stand in need of comfort.
r.comment: Fellowship enacted: to bear one another’s burdens and mourn with those that mourn.

r.text: Wherefore, I give unto them a commandment, saying thus: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, with all thy might, mind, and strength; and in the name of Jesus Christ thou shalt serve him. Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself.
r.comment: The two loves in Restoration voice: love God, and love thy neighbor.

r.text: And there shall be mine abode, and it shall be Zion, which shall come forth out of all the creations which I have made; and for the space of a thousand years the earth shall rest.
r.comment: The promised end: His abode with His people, called Zion.

s3.tx: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
s3.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:1, the film's Christological hinge. D&C 93:8 is set beside it as a Restoration restatement, confirming rather than extending the Johannine claim.

b.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

r.text: Therefore, in the beginning the Word was, for he was the Word, even the messenger of salvation—
r.comment: Restoration restatement of the Johannine 'Word.'

s4.tx: The same was in the beginning with God.
s4.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:2, holding the Word with God before the creative acts begin. 3 Nephi 9:15 sets the risen Christ's own testimony beside it—that He was 'with the Father from the beginning'—as a Restoration witness that the Word of the prologue and the Savior are one, confirming the Johannine claim rather than arguing it.

b.text: The same was in the beginning with God.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

r.text: Behold, I am Jesus Christ the Son of God. I created the heavens and the earth, and all things that in them are. I was with the Father from the beginning. I am in the Father, and the Father in me; and in me hath the Father glorified his name.
r.comment: The risen Christ names Himself Creator and 'with the Father from the beginning'; offered as convergent witness, not premise.

s5.tx: All things were made by Him, and without Him was not anything made that was made.
s5.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:3, with Colossians 1:16 widening the scope of the Word's creative agency. Moses 1:32 confirms the same agency in Restoration language.

b.text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

b.text: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:
b.comment: Widens the scope of the Word's creative agency.

r.text: And by the word of my power, have I created them, which is mine Only Begotten Son, who is full of grace and truth.
r.comment: Creation by the word, through the Son.

s6.tx: In the Word was life, and that life was the light of men.
s6.pc: Near-verbatim John 1:4; the narration substitutes 'the Word' for the pronoun to keep the referent plain. Doctrine and Covenants 93:9 echoes the same pairing of life and light in Restoration language—'in him was the life of men and the light of men'—a restatement, not an addition.

b.text: In him was life; and the life was the light of men.
b.comment: The verse the narration renders, with 'the Word' supplied for the pronoun.

r.text: The light and the Redeemer of the world; the Spirit of truth, who came into the world, because the world was made by him, and in him was the life of men and the light of men.
r.comment: Restoration restatement pairing life and light in the Word.

s7.tx: His light shineth in darkness, and the darkness comprehended it not.
s7.pc: Near-verbatim John 1:5. Doctrine and Covenants 88:49 restates it almost word for word and turns it toward promise—'the day shall come when you shall comprehend even God'—confirming the image while extending its hope.

b.text: And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.
b.comment: Quoted, lightly adapted ('His light').

r.text: The light shineth in darkness, and the darkness comprehendeth it not; nevertheless, the day shall come when you shall comprehend even God, being quickened in him and by him.
r.comment: Near-verbatim restatement, carried toward the eventual comprehension of God.

s8.tx: The Word of God spoke the heavens and the earth into being.
s8.pc: A compression of the whole 'He spake, and it was done' witness. Psalm 33:6 and 33:9 supply the biblical ground—the heavens made by the word, done at His speaking—with Hebrews 11:3 naming the worlds framed by God's word and 2 Peter 3:5 recalling that by that word the heavens were of old. Jacob 4:9 is the Restoration's own creation-by-word verse, confirming that what the Word spoke, was.

b.text: By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; and all the host of them by the breath of his mouth.
b.comment: The heavens made by the word of the LORD.

b.text: For he spake, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast.
b.comment: 'He spake, and it was done'—the creative word enacted.

b.text: Through faith we understand that the worlds were framed by the word of God, so that things which are seen were not made of things which do appear.
b.comment: The worlds framed by the word of God.

b.text: For this they willingly are ignorant of, that by the word of God the heavens were of old, and the earth standing out of the water and in the water:
b.comment: By the word of God the heavens were of old.

r.text: For behold, by the power of his word man came upon the face of the earth, which earth was created by the power of his word.
r.comment: Creation by the power of His word, in Restoration voice.

s9.tx: [ ♫ music ♫ ] But the earth was without form and void.
s9.pc: Genesis 1:2, first clause. Moses 2:2 gives the same in first-person Restoration voice, and Abraham 4:2 in the language of the Gods ('empty and desolate'); the three accounts converge on one scene. Genesis 1:2 carries s9 through s11, each span rendering one clause of the single verse.

b.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
b.comment: 'Without form, and void'—the opening condition of the earth.

r.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and I caused darkness to come up upon the face of the deep; and my Spirit moved upon the face of the water; for I am God.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the earth, after it was formed, was empty and desolate, because they had not formed anything but the earth; and darkness reigned upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of the Gods was brooding upon the face of the waters.
r.comment: The account of the Gods: 'empty and desolate.'

s10.tx: Darkness was upon the face of the deep.
s10.pc: Genesis 1:2, second clause—darkness over the deep. Moses 2:2 and Abraham 4:2 stand as the same Restoration witnesses; the anchor is the one verse's next clause, not a new event.

b.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
b.comment: 'Darkness was upon the face of the deep.'

r.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and I caused darkness to come up upon the face of the deep; and my Spirit moved upon the face of the water; for I am God.
r.comment: Restoration parallel (darkness over the deep).

r.text: And the earth, after it was formed, was empty and desolate, because they had not formed anything but the earth; and darkness reigned upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of the Gods was brooding upon the face of the waters.
r.comment: 'Darkness reigned upon the face of the deep.'

s11.tx: [ ♫ music ♫ ] The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
s11.pc: Genesis 1:2, final clause—the Spirit upon the waters. Moses 2:2 renders it 'my Spirit moved upon the face of the water'; Abraham 4:2 'brooding upon the face of the waters'—the Restoration accounts vary the image without altering the scene.

b.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
b.comment: 'The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.'

r.text: And the earth was without form, and void; and I caused darkness to come up upon the face of the deep; and my Spirit moved upon the face of the water; for I am God.
r.comment: 'My Spirit moved upon the face of the water.'

r.text: And the earth, after it was formed, was empty and desolate, because they had not formed anything but the earth; and darkness reigned upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of the Gods was brooding upon the face of the waters.
r.comment: 'Brooding upon the face of the waters.'

s12.pc: Genesis 1:3, the first creative command. Moses 2:3 and Abraham 4:3 confirm the identical command—'Let there be light; and there was light'—across the three accounts.

b.text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
b.comment: The first spoken command of creation.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let there be light; and there was light.
r.comment: Restoration parallel, first person.

r.text: And they (the Gods) said: Let there be light; and there was light.
r.comment: The Gods speak the same command.

s13.tx: And He divided the light from the darkness, saying, “Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters to divide the waters from the waters.” And God called the firmament heaven.
s13.pc: Three Genesis verses compressed into one beat: the dividing of light from darkness (1:4), the firmament in the midst of the waters (1:6), and its naming as Heaven (1:8). Moses 2:6-8 tracks the same acts in first-person voice; Abraham 4:6-8 renders the firmament as an 'expanse' the Gods order until obeyed.

b.text: And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
b.comment: God divides the light from the darkness.

b.text: And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
b.comment: The firmament in the midst of the waters.

b.text: And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
b.comment: The firmament called Heaven; the second day.

r.text: And again, I, God, said: Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and it was so, even as I spake; and I said: Let it divide the waters from the waters; and it was done;
r.comment: Restoration parallel: the firmament, first person.

r.text: And I, God, called the firmament Heaven; and the evening and the morning were the second day.
r.comment: 'I, God, called the firmament Heaven.'

r.text: And the Gods also said: Let there be an expanse in the midst of the waters, and it shall divide the waters from the waters.
r.comment: Abraham's account: an 'expanse' in the midst of the waters.

r.text: And the Gods called the expanse, Heaven. And it came to pass that it was from evening until morning that they called night; and it came to pass that it was from morning until evening that they called day; and this was the second time that they called night and day.
r.comment: The Gods name the expanse Heaven.

s14.tx: [ ♫ music ♫ ] God spoke again, “Let the waters be gathered into one place, and let the dry land appear.”
s14.pc: Genesis 1:9—the waters gathered, dry land appearing. Moses 2:9 and Abraham 4:9 give the Restoration parallels; Abraham's 'and it was so as they ordered' carries that account's distinctive obedience refrain.

b.text: And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
b.comment: The waters gathered; the dry land appears.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and it was so; and I, God, said: Let there be dry land; and it was so.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the Gods ordered, saying: Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the earth come up dry; and it was so as they ordered;
r.comment: The Gods order; 'it was so as they ordered.'

s15.tx: And God called the dry land earth.
s15.pc: Genesis 1:10, first clause—the naming of the dry land Earth. Moses 2:10 and Abraham 4:10 confirm; Genesis 1:10 carries both s15 and s16, split at its two naming-clauses.

b.text: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
b.comment: 'God called the dry land Earth.'

r.text: And I, God, called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, called I the Sea; and I, God, saw that all things which I had made were good.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the Gods pronounced the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, pronounced they, Great Waters; and the Gods saw that they were obeyed.
r.comment: The Gods 'pronounced' the land and waters.

s16.tx: The gathering together of the waters called He seas.
s16.pc: Genesis 1:10, second clause—the gathered waters called Seas. The same Moses 2:10 and Abraham 4:10 witnesses stand; the anchor is the verse's next naming-clause, not a new act.

b.text: And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
b.comment: 'The gathering together of the waters called he Seas.'

r.text: And I, God, called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, called I the Sea; and I, God, saw that all things which I had made were good.
r.comment: Restoration parallel (the seas).

r.text: And the Gods pronounced the dry land, Earth; and the gathering together of the waters, pronounced they, Great Waters; and the Gods saw that they were obeyed.
r.comment: The Gods pronounce the waters 'Great Waters.'

s17.tx: God, the Father of Spirits, gathered a Divine Council of heavenly beings.
s17.pc: Scripture repeatedly shows God amid a heavenly council. The host stands by His throne (1 Kings 22:19); the sons of God present themselves before Him (Job 1:6); the assembly of the holy ones surrounds Him (Psalm 89). Restoration scripture names it: the Council of the Eternal God before this world was (Doctrine and Covenants 121:32), the noble and great ones organized before the world (Abraham 3:22–23), the seraphic hosts of heaven before the world was made (Doctrine and Covenants 38:1). 'Father of Spirits' carries from Hebrews 12:9.

b.text: And he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.
b.comment: The LORD enthroned amid all the host of heaven — the council seen.

b.text: Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD…
b.comment: The sons of God presenting themselves before the LORD — the heavenly court assembled.

b.text: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
b.comment: God presiding in the divine assembly.

b.text: And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O LORD: thy faithfulness also in the congregation of the saints… God is greatly to be feared in the assembly of the saints, and to be had in reverence of all them that are about him.
b.comment: The assembly of the holy ones gathered about the LORD.

b.text: For who hath stood in the counsel of the LORD, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it?
b.comment: The prophetic 'counsel of the LORD' — the divine deliberative assembly.

b.text: A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.
b.comment: Ten thousand times ten thousand of the heavenly host standing before Him.

r.text: Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.
r.comment: The noble and great ones organized before the world; God stood in the midst of the assembly.

r.text: According to that which was ordained in the midst of the Council of the Eternal God of all other gods before this world was, that should be reserved unto the finishing and the end thereof, when every man shall enter into his eternal presence and into his immortal rest.
r.comment: Named plainly: the Council of the Eternal God, before this world was.

r.text: Thus saith the Lord your God, even Jesus Christ, the Great I Am, Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the same which looked upon the wide expanse of eternity, and all the seraphic hosts of heaven, before the world was made;
r.comment: Christ beheld all the seraphic hosts of heaven before the world was made.

s19.tx: “When I laid the foundations of the earth.
s19.pc: The Lord answers Job out of the whirlwind by pointing back to the founding of the earth — a work the heavenly host witnessed and no mortal saw (Job 38:4). The same laying of the earth's foundations is sung across the Psalms and the Prophets.

b.text: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? declare, if thou hast understanding.
b.comment: The Lord's question to Job — the words the narration renders.

b.text: Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.
b.comment: The LORD who laid the earth's foundations.

b.text: When he gave to the sea his decree, that the waters should not pass his commandment: when he appointed the foundations of the earth:
b.comment: Present when He appointed the foundations of the earth.

b.text: Mine hand also hath laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand hath spanned the heavens: when I call unto them, they stand up together.
b.comment: The LORD's own hand laid the earth's foundation.

s20.tx: The morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy.”
s20.pc: Job 38:7, quoted almost word for word — the heavenly host rejoicing as the earth was founded. Joseph Smith takes up the same words as praise (Doctrine and Covenants 128:23), calling the morning stars and the sons of God to sing and shout again.

b.text: When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
b.comment: The verse the narration renders — the hosts rejoicing at the founding.

r.text: …And let the sun, moon, and the morning stars sing together, and let all the sons of God shout for joy! And let the eternal creations declare his name forever and ever!
r.comment: Joseph Smith takes up Job's words as praise — the morning stars and sons of God called to sing and shout again.

s21.tx: The first among them was the WORD, the First Born of every creature, the express image of the Father.
s21.pc: Among the council, one is preeminent — the Word (John 1:1). Scripture names Him the firstborn of every creature and the image of the invisible God (Colossians 1:15), the express image of the Father's person (Hebrews 1:3), and the bright and morning star (Revelation 22:16) — first among the morning stars just heard singing. Restoration scripture calls Him plainly the Firstborn (Doctrine and Covenants 93:21) and shows Him standing in the council as the one like unto God who led the creation (Abraham 3:24).

b.text: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:
b.comment: Both titles in one verse: the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.

b.text: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
b.comment: 'The express image of his person' — the phrase the narration renders.

b.text: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.
b.comment: Christ the bright and morning star — first among the morning stars just heard.

r.text: And now, verily I say unto you, I was in the beginning with the Father, and am the Firstborn;
r.comment: Christ's own words: 'I was in the beginning with the Father, and am the Firstborn.'

r.text: And there stood one among them that was like unto God, and he said unto those who were with him: We will go down, for there is space there, and we will take of these materials, and we will make an earth whereon these may dwell;
r.comment: The one 'like unto God' standing preeminent in the council, who led the creation.

s22.tx: This same Word would be born as Jesus of Nazareth.
s22.pc: The premortal Word now named. The one who was in the form of God would be made in the likeness of men (Philippians 2:6-7), sent forth in the fulness of time, made of a woman (Galatians 4:4), and called JESUS, Son of the Highest, heir to the throne of David (Luke 1:31-33). The universal Christian claim stands first—Emmanuel, God with us (Matthew 1:23)—while the distinctively Restoration naming of Jehovah as Jesus is held for s65. Restoration scripture confirms the same identity: the Creator of all things from the beginning, born of Mary (Mosiah 3:8), and God Himself come down among men to redeem them (Mosiah 15:1).

b.text: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:
b.comment: The pre-existent one in the form of God, made in the likeness of men.

b.text: But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,
b.comment: The Son sent forth in the fulness of time, made of a woman.

b.text: And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS. He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
b.comment: The naming: JESUS, Son of the Highest, given the throne of David.

b.text: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us.
b.comment: Emmanuel, God with us—the incarnate name.

r.text: And he shall be called Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Father of heaven and earth, the Creator of all things from the beginning; and his mother shall be called Mary.
r.comment: The Creator of all things from the beginning, named Jesus Christ and born of Mary.

r.text: And now Abinadi said unto them: I would that ye should understand that God himself shall come down among the children of men, and shall redeem his people.
r.comment: God Himself come down among the children of men to redeem His people.

s23.tx: The Word was made flesh and dwelt among us.
s23.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:14, the incarnation stated plainly; the narration renders it through 'dwelt among us.' Doctrine and Covenants 93:11 restates it in John's own voice—the Only Begotten, full of grace and truth, which came and dwelt in the flesh and dwelt among us. Mosiah 15:2 supplies the reason the incarnate Word is called the Son: because he dwelleth in flesh. Restatements of the one claim, not additions to it.

b.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
b.comment: Quoted in the narration through 'dwelt among us.'

r.text: And I, John, bear record that I beheld his glory, as the glory of the Only Begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth, even the Spirit of truth, which came and dwelt in the flesh, and dwelt among us.
r.comment: Restoration restatement in John's own voice: came and dwelt in the flesh, and dwelt among us.

r.text: And because he dwelleth in flesh he shall be called the Son of God, and having subjected the flesh to the will of the Father, being the Father and the Son—
r.comment: Because He dwelleth in flesh He shall be called the Son of God.

s24.tx: He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not.
s24.pc: Direct quotation of John 1:10, the film's Christological irony: the world made by Him did not know Him. John 1:11 completes the thought—his own received him not. Doctrine and Covenants 93:10 gives the Restoration witness to the making (the worlds were made by him), kept distinct from the life-and-light verse already set at s6 (93:9). Mosiah 3:9 carries the not-knowing: even after all He did, they shall consider him a man.

b.text: He was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.
b.comment: Quoted verbatim in the narration.

b.text: He came unto his own, and his own received him not.
b.comment: The completing clause: His own received Him not.

r.text: The worlds were made by him; men were made by him; all things were made by him, and through him, and of him.
r.comment: Restoration witness to the worlds made by Him; distinct from 93:9 at s6.

r.text: And lo, he cometh unto his own, that salvation might come unto the children of men even through faith on his name; and even after all this they shall consider him a man, and say that he hath a devil, and shall scourge him, and shall crucify him.
r.comment: The world's not-knowing foretold: they shall consider him a man.

s25.tx: Of the Father are all things.
s25.pc: A compression of 1 Corinthians 8:6—one God, the Father, of whom are all things—naming the Father as the source from whom all things come. The verse's companion clause, one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, is the very structure the next span voices (s26). Moses 1:33 gives the Restoration witness, joining Father-source and Son-agent in one line.

b.text: But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.
b.comment: 'Of whom are all things'—the Father as source; the Son-agent clause is voiced at s26.

r.text: And worlds without number have I created; and I also created them for mine own purpose; and by the Son I created them, which is mine Only Begotten.
r.comment: Father as source, created for His own purpose; and by the Son the creating is done.

s26.tx: And by the Son in heaven and in earth, visible and invisible, all things were created by Him, and for Him, and by Him all things consist.
s26.pc: The narration is Colossians 1:16-17 rendered nearly word for word: all things in heaven and earth, visible and invisible, created by Him and for Him, and by Him all things consist. Colossians 1:16 was set earlier at s5 to widen John 1:3's 'all things'; here the couplet is the narration's own source, carried through v17's word of sustaining—not origin only, but holding-together. Restoration witnesses: Mosiah 4:9 (he created all things, both in heaven and in earth) and Doctrine and Covenants 88:41, which reaches past creation to immanence—God in all things, through all things, and round about all things.

b.text: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
b.comment: The couplet the narration renders; v17 adds 'by him all things consist.' Colossians 1:16 also stands at s5, there widening John 1:3.

r.text: Believe in God; believe that he is, and that he created all things, both in heaven and in earth; believe that he has all wisdom, and all power, both in heaven and in earth; believe that man doth not comprehend all the things which the Lord can comprehend.
r.comment: He created all things, both in heaven and in earth.

r.text: He comprehendeth all things, and all things are before him, and all things are round about him; and he is above all things, and in all things, and is through all things, and is round about all things; and all things are by him, and of him, even God, forever and ever.
r.comment: Past origin to sustaining: by him and of him—the all things consist witness.

s27.tx: He is before all things the Heir of all things, by whom God the Father made the worlds.
s27.pc: Hebrews 1:2 supplies the span's distinctive content: the Son appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds. The opening clause, 'He is before all things,' restates Colossians 1:17 already carried at s26, so the biblical anchor rests on Hebrews. Psalm 2:8 gives the Old Testament root of the inheritance. Doctrine and Covenants 76:24 is the Restoration witness: by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created.

b.text: Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
b.comment: Heir of all things, by whom He made the worlds—the phrase the narration renders.

b.text: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.
b.comment: The Old Testament root of the Son's inheritance.

r.text: That by him, and through him, and of him, the worlds are and were created, and the inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters unto God.
r.comment: By Him the worlds were created—the Restoration witness to the making.

s28.tx: The Word commanded, “Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide day from night.
s28.pc: The fourth creative period opens. Genesis 1:14 speaks the command—lights in the firmament to divide day from night—and the narration renders its first clause. As with the earlier creative days (s9-s16), the three accounts run in parallel: Moses 2:14 in first-person voice, and Abraham 4:14 in the language of the Gods, who organized the lights in the expanse of the heaven. Genesis 1:14 carries s28 and s29, split at its two clauses—the dividing here, the signs and seasons next.

b.text: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:
b.comment: The creative command the narration renders; its first clause divides day from night.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven, to divide the day from the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and for years;
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the Gods organized the lights in the expanse of the heaven, and caused them to divide the day from the night; and organized them to be for signs and for seasons, and for days and for years;
r.comment: The account of the Gods: they 'organized the lights in the expanse of the heaven.'

s29.tx: Let them be for signs and for seasons, for days and for years.”
s29.pc: Genesis 1:14, second clause—the lights appointed for signs and seasons, for days and years; the anchor is the verse's next clause, not a new act. Psalm 104:19 sounds the same note in praise: 'He appointed the moon for seasons.' Moses 2:14 and Abraham 4:14 carry the Restoration parallels, each ordering the lights for signs and for seasons, for days and for years.

b.text: And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:
b.comment: 'For signs, and for seasons'—the second clause of the same verse.

b.text: He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.
b.comment: The seasons-keeping of the luminaries, sung in the psalm.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven, to divide the day from the night, and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and for years;
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel (signs and seasons).

r.text: And the Gods organized the lights in the expanse of the heaven, and caused them to divide the day from the night; and organized them to be for signs and for seasons, and for days and for years;
r.comment: The Gods order the lights for signs and seasons.

s30.tx: Two lights were made to shine.
s30.pc: A light paraphrase of Genesis 1:16—'God made two great lights.' The narration compresses 'two great lights' into 'two lights ... made to shine.' Moses 2:16 gives the first-person parallel, naming the sun and the moon; Abraham 4:16, the account of the Gods, who organized the two great lights. Genesis 1:16 carries s30 through s32, split at its clauses.

b.text: And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
b.comment: 'God made two great lights'—the clause the narration compresses.

r.text: And I, God, made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the greater light was the sun, and the lesser light was the moon; and the stars also were made even according to my word.
r.comment: First-person Restoration parallel.

r.text: And the Gods organized the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; with the lesser light they set the stars also;
r.comment: The Gods 'organized the two great lights.'

s31.tx: The greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night.
s31.pc: Genesis 1:16, second clause, quoted almost word for word—the greater light to rule the day, the lesser to rule the night. Psalm 136:8-9 sets the same rule in the cadence of praise: the sun to rule by day, the moon and stars to rule by night. Moses 2:16 names the two lights the sun and the moon; Abraham 4:16 reads 'with the lesser light they set the stars also.'

b.text: And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
b.comment: The greater and lesser lights—the verse's ruling clause.

b.text: The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.
b.comment: The same rule in the psalm of praise: the sun by day, the moon and stars by night.

r.text: And I, God, made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the greater light was the sun, and the lesser light was the moon; and the stars also were made even according to my word.
r.comment: 'The greater light was the sun, and the lesser light was the moon.'

r.text: And the Gods organized the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; with the lesser light they set the stars also;
r.comment: The greater and lesser lights ordered to rule day and night.

s32.pc: Genesis 1:16, final clause, verbatim—'he made the stars also.' The plain clause is kept plain here; the stars' fuller praise, numbered and called by name, is gathered in the closing prayer. Moses 2:16 adds that 'the stars also were made even according to my word'; Abraham 4:16, 'with the lesser light they set the stars also.'

b.text: And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
b.comment: 'He made the stars also'—quoted verbatim, the verse's final clause.

r.text: And I, God, made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night, and the greater light was the sun, and the lesser light was the moon; and the stars also were made even according to my word.
r.comment: 'The stars also were made even according to my word.'

r.text: And the Gods organized the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night; with the lesser light they set the stars also;
r.comment: 'With the lesser light they set the stars also.'

s33.tx: God did not create the earth in vain.
s33.pc: The narration turns from the lights to their purpose, rendering Isaiah 45:18—the LORD who formed the earth 'created it not in vain.' The verse carries s33 and s34, split at its two clauses: the earth not made in vain here, formed to be inhabited next. Doctrine and Covenants 104:17 confirms the fulness of that purpose—the earth 'full, and there is enough and to spare,' the Creator having prepared all things for His children.

b.text: For thus saith the LORD that created the heavens; God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else.
b.comment: 'He created it not in vain'—the clause the narration renders; the verse continues into s34.

r.text: For the earth is full, and there is enough and to spare; yea, I prepared all things, and have given unto the children of men to be agents unto themselves.
r.comment: The earth prepared full and sufficient—'enough and to spare,' not made in vain.

s34.tx: He formed it to be inhabited.
s34.pc: Isaiah 45:18, its closing clause—the earth 'formed to be inhabited.' The anchor is the verse's next clause, not a new act. 1 Nephi 17:36 gives the Restoration witness almost word for word: the Lord created the earth that it should be inhabited, and created His children that they should possess it.

b.text: For thus saith the LORD that created the heavens; God himself that formed the earth and made it; he hath established it, he created it not in vain, he formed it to be inhabited: I am the LORD; and there is none else.
b.comment: 'He formed it to be inhabited'—the closing clause of the same verse.

r.text: Behold, the Lord hath created the earth that it should be inhabited; and he hath created his children that they should possess it.
r.comment: Near-verbatim Restoration witness: created the earth that it should be inhabited.

s36.tx: “Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life: great whales, and every living creature that moves, which the waters brought forth abundantly.”
s36.pc: The fifth day. The narration renders Genesis 1:20-21 nearly whole—the command that the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature (1:20), and its fulfillment, the great whales and every living creature the waters brought forth (1:21). The three accounts run in parallel: Moses 2:20-21 in first-person voice, and Abraham 4:20-21 in the planning language of the Gods, who 'prepare the waters' to bring them forth. The fowl clause of Genesis 1:20 is held for s38, where the narration gathers the creatures of the air.

b.text: And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
b.comment: The command: let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature. Its fowl clause is carried at s38.

b.text: And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.
b.comment: The fulfillment: great whales and every living creature the waters brought forth.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl which may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
r.comment: First-person parallel to the command.

r.text: And I, God, created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind; and I, God, saw that all things which I had created were good.
r.comment: First-person parallel to the making of the whales.

r.text: And the Gods said: Let us prepare the waters to bring forth abundantly the moving creatures that have life; and the fowl, that they may fly above the earth in the open expanse of heaven.
r.comment: The Gods 'prepare the waters'—the planning voice of the Abraham account.

r.text: And the Gods prepared the waters that they might bring forth great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters were to bring forth abundantly after their kind; and every winged fowl after their kind. And the Gods saw that they would be obeyed, and that their plan was good.
r.comment: The Gods prepared the waters to bring forth great whales; 'their plan was good.'

s37.tx: “Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the tree yielding fruit.” And God blessed them all, saying, “Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas.”
s37.pc: Two acts in one breath. First the earth is commanded to bring forth grass, herb, and fruit tree (Genesis 1:11)—the film gathers the vegetation here, by habitat rather than by the order of the days. Then the blessing upon the living creatures of the sea: be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters (Genesis 1:22). Each act carries its three-account witness—Moses 2:11 and Abraham 4:11 for the plants, Moses 2:22 and Abraham 4:22 for the blessing. The 'let fowl multiply' clause of Genesis 1:22 returns at s39.

b.text: And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.
b.comment: The command for grass, herb, and fruit tree, each yielding seed after its kind.

b.text: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.
b.comment: The blessing: be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, the fruit tree yielding fruit, after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed should be in itself upon the earth, and it was so even as I spake.
r.comment: First-person parallel for the vegetation.

r.text: And the Gods said: Let us prepare the earth to bring forth grass; the herb yielding seed; the fruit tree yielding fruit, after his kind, whose seed in itself yieldeth its own likeness upon the earth; and it was so, even as they ordered.
r.comment: The Gods 'prepare the earth to bring forth grass.'

r.text: And I, God, blessed them, saying: Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the sea; and let fowl multiply in the earth;
r.comment: First-person parallel to the blessing (Moses reads 'fill the waters in the sea').

r.text: And the Gods said: We will bless them, and cause them to be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas or great waters; and cause the fowl to multiply in the earth.
r.comment: The Gods 'will bless them'—the planning voice; 'fill the waters in the seas or great waters.'

s38.tx: “Let the earth bring forth living creatures, the cattle, and creeping things, and beasts of the earth, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
s38.pc: The sixth day's living creatures—cattle, creeping things, and beasts of the earth (Genesis 1:24)—joined to the winged fowl the film held back from s36. That fowl clause is the second half of Genesis 1:20, returned here where the narration gathers the creatures of the air with those of the land. Moses 2:24 and Abraham 4:24 give the three-account witness for the land creatures; Moses 2:20 and Abraham 4:20 carry the fowl, reasserted from s36 in its own place.

b.text: And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.
b.comment: The land creatures: cattle, creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind.

b.text: And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
b.comment: The fowl clause of Genesis 1:20, held from s36 and rendered here.

r.text: And I, God, said: Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping things, and beasts of the earth after their kind, and it was so;
r.comment: First-person parallel for the land creatures.

r.text: And the Gods prepared the earth to bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle and creeping things, and beasts of the earth after their kind; and it was so, as they had said.
r.comment: The Gods 'prepare the earth to bring forth the living creature.'

r.text: And I, God, said: Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl which may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
r.comment: The fowl 'which may fly above the earth'—reasserted from s36.

r.text: And the Gods said: Let us prepare the waters to bring forth abundantly the moving creatures that have life; and the fowl, that they may fly above the earth in the open expanse of heaven.
r.comment: The Gods prepare 'the fowl, that they may fly above the earth'—reasserted from s36.

s39.tx: Let them multiply upon the earth.”
s39.pc: A paraphrase gathering the blessing's increase—'let them multiply upon the earth.' The words compress the close of Genesis 1:22, 'let fowl multiply in the earth,' widened from the fowl to all the living creatures just named. The verse and its three-account witnesses (Moses 2:22, Abraham 4:22) are reasserted from s37: there the blessing filled the waters; here the same blessing fills the earth.

b.text: And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.
b.comment: 'Let fowl multiply in the earth'—the multiply clause, reasserted from s37 and widened to all the creatures.

r.text: And I, God, blessed them, saying: Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the sea; and let fowl multiply in the earth;
r.comment: First-person parallel; reasserted from s37.

r.text: And the Gods said: We will bless them, and cause them to be fruitful and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas or great waters; and cause the fowl to multiply in the earth.
r.comment: The Gods 'cause the fowl to multiply in the earth'—reasserted from s37.

s40.tx: Then God the Father said to the Divine council, “Let us make man in Our image, after Our likeness, male and female.”
s40.pc: The making of man, spoken in the plural. The narration renders 'Let us make man in our image, after our likeness' (Genesis 1:26), joined to 'male and female' (Genesis 1:27)—both reasserted from s2b, where they ground the relational purpose of our creation; here they mark the creative act itself, spoken within the council already seen at s17. On-screen the 'us' is left open, as Genesis leaves it. The Restoration accounts name the council more fully: Moses 2:26 has God speak 'unto mine Only Begotten, which was with me from the beginning,' and Abraham 4:26 has 'the Gods' take counsel among themselves and go down to form man—the preeminent Word of s21 now at the work. Moses 2:27 and Abraham 4:27 carry 'male and female'; Moses 6:9 (reasserted from s2b) confirms the image is embodied. These stand as additional witness to the plural 'us,' deepening the Genesis council rather than settling how it is read.

b.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
b.comment: The council command, made in our image; reasserted from s2b—there the relational purpose, here the creative act.

b.text: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
b.comment: 'Male and female created he them'; reasserted from s2b.

b.text: This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him;
b.comment: The likeness restated: made in the likeness of God.

r.text: And I, God, said unto mine Only Begotten, which was with me from the beginning: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; and it was so. And I, God, said: Let them have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
r.comment: The council named: God speaks unto the Only Begotten who was with Him from the beginning.

r.text: And I, God, created man in mine own image, in the image of mine Only Begotten created I him; male and female created I them.
r.comment: Man created in the image of the Only Begotten; male and female.

r.text: And the Gods took counsel among themselves and said: Let us go down and form man in our image, after our likeness; and we will give them dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
r.comment: The Gods take counsel and go down to form man—the account's council language.

r.text: So the Gods went down to organize man in their own image, in the image of the Gods to form they him, male and female to form they them.
r.comment: The Gods go down to organize man, male and female.

r.text: In the image of his own body, male and female, created he them, and blessed them, and called their name Adam, in the day when they were created and became living souls in the land upon the footstool of God.
r.comment: The image is embodied—male and female; reasserted from s2b.

s41.tx: He formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into him the breath of life.
s41.pc: Genesis 2:7, its opening clauses—man formed of dust, the breath of life breathed in. Genesis 2:7 carries s41 and s42, split at the making here and the living soul next. Job 33:4 sounds the same breath in the cadence of witness. Moses 3:7 gives the first-person parallel, adding that man was 'the first flesh upon the earth'; Abraham 5:7 renders it distinctively—the Gods 'took his spirit... and put it into him,' then breathed the breath of life.

b.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
b.comment: Man formed of dust, the breath of life breathed in; the verse continues into s42.

b.text: The Spirit of God hath made me, and the breath of the Almighty hath given me life.
b.comment: The breath of the Almighty giving life, in the voice of witness.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul, the first flesh upon the earth, the first man also; nevertheless, all things were before created; but spiritually were they created and made according to my word.
r.comment: First-person parallel; man 'the first flesh upon the earth.' Carries s42.

r.text: And the Gods formed man from the dust of the ground, and took his spirit (that is, the man’s spirit), and put it into him; and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.
r.comment: Distinctive: the Gods took his spirit and put it into him. Carries s42.

s42.tx: And man became a living soul.
s42.pc: Genesis 2:7, its closing clause—'and man became a living soul' (reasserted from s41). Paul takes up the words in 1 Corinthians 15:45, 'the first man Adam was made a living soul,' and carries them toward Christ, the last Adam, a quickening spirit. Moses 3:7 and Abraham 5:7 (both reasserted from s41) give the Restoration witness to the same living soul.

b.text: And the LORD God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
b.comment: 'And man became a living soul'—the verse's closing clause, reasserted from s41.

b.text: And so it is written, The first man Adam was made a living soul; the last Adam was made a quickening spirit.
b.comment: Paul carries the living soul toward Christ, the last Adam, a quickening spirit.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul, the first flesh upon the earth, the first man also; nevertheless, all things were before created; but spiritually were they created and made according to my word.
r.comment: 'Man became a living soul'; reasserted from s41.

r.text: And the Gods formed man from the dust of the ground, and took his spirit (that is, the man’s spirit), and put it into him; and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul.
r.comment: 'Man became a living soul'; reasserted from s41.

s43.tx: And God planted a garden eastward in Eden.
s43.pc: Genesis 2:8, its first clause—the Lord God plants a garden eastward in Eden. Genesis 2:8 carries s43 and s44, split at the planting here and the placing of the man next. Moses 3:8 gives the first-person parallel; Abraham 5:8, the account of the Gods, who put the man 'whose spirit they had put into the body which they had formed.'

b.text: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.
b.comment: The garden planted eastward in Eden; the verse continues into s44.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, planted a garden eastward in Eden, and there I put the man whom I had formed.
r.comment: First-person parallel; carries s44.

r.text: And the Gods planted a garden, eastward in Eden, and there they put the man, whose spirit they had put into the body which they had formed.
r.comment: The Gods plant the garden and place the man whose spirit they had put into the body. Carries s44.

s44.tx: And there he put the man whom he had formed to dress it and to keep it.
s44.pc: Two clauses joined: the placing of the man (Genesis 2:8, reasserted from s43) and his charge to dress and keep the garden (Genesis 2:15). Moses 3:8 (reasserted from s43) and Moses 3:15 carry the Restoration parallel; Abraham 5:8 (reasserted from s43) and Abraham 5:11 the account of the Gods, who took the man and put him in Eden to dress it and to keep it.

b.text: And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.
b.comment: 'There he put the man whom he had formed'; reasserted from s43.

b.text: And the LORD God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
b.comment: The charge: to dress it and to keep it.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, planted a garden eastward in Eden, and there I put the man whom I had formed.
r.comment: The placing of the man; reasserted from s43.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, took the man, and put him into the Garden of Eden, to dress it, and to keep it.
r.comment: 'To dress it, and to keep it.'

r.text: And the Gods planted a garden, eastward in Eden, and there they put the man, whose spirit they had put into the body which they had formed.
r.comment: The placing of the man; reasserted from s43.

r.text: And the Gods took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden, to dress it and to keep it.
r.comment: The Gods put the man in Eden to dress it and to keep it.

s45.tx: The father said, “It is not good that the man should be alone.”
s45.pc: Genesis 2:18 (reasserted from s2b, where it grounds our being made for relationship; here the moment in the garden that prompts the making of the woman). The Restoration accounts again name the council: Moses 3:18 has God speak 'unto mine Only Begotten' that it was not good for the man to be alone; Abraham 5:14 has the Gods say, 'Let us make an help meet for the man.' Additional witness to the plural voice, set beside the plain Genesis word.

b.text: And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.
b.comment: 'It is not good that the man should be alone'; reasserted from s2b.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, said unto mine Only Begotten, that it was not good that the man should be alone; wherefore, I will make an help meet for him.
r.comment: Spoken unto the Only Begotten.

r.text: And the Gods said: Let us make an help meet for the man, for it is not good that the man should be alone, therefore we will form an help meet for him.
r.comment: 'Let us make an help meet for the man.'

s46.tx: So He made a woman and brought her unto the man, explaining, “Therefore shall a man cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.”
s46.pc: The making of the woman (Genesis 2:22) and the word of one flesh (Genesis 2:24). Christ Himself binds the two when questioned on marriage, citing the creation: 'he which made them at the beginning made them male and female'—the very word of s40—'and they twain shall be one flesh' (Matthew 19:4-6); Paul repeats it in Ephesians 5:31. Moses 3:22 and 3:24 give the Restoration parallel; Abraham 5:16-18 the account of the Gods, closing on the same one flesh. Genesis 2:23 and Moses 3:23, the naming 'bone of my bones,' stand between as the hinge to the one-flesh word.

b.text: And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.
b.comment: The woman made of the rib and brought unto the man.

b.text: And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.
b.comment: The naming—the hinge to one flesh.

b.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
b.comment: The word the narration quotes: cleave, and one flesh.

b.text: And he answered and said unto them, Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder.
b.comment: Christ cites the creation—male and female, and one flesh—the word of s40 carried into His teaching.

b.text: For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh.
b.comment: Paul repeats the one-flesh word of Genesis.

r.text: And the rib which I, the Lord God, had taken from man, made I a woman, and brought her unto the man.
r.comment: The woman made and brought unto the man.

r.text: And Adam said: This I know now is bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of man.
r.comment: The naming—'bone of my bones.'

r.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife; and they shall be one flesh.
r.comment: Cleave, and one flesh.

r.text: And of the rib which the Gods had taken from man, formed they a woman, and brought her unto the man.
r.comment: The Gods form the woman of the rib and bring her unto the man.

r.text: And Adam said: This was bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh; now she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of man;
r.comment: The naming in the account of the Gods.

r.text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife, and they shall be one flesh.
r.comment: The same close: cleave, and one flesh.

s47.tx: And God commanded, “Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing upon the earth.” God blessed them, and said unto them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and have dominion over all life.”
s47.pc: Genesis 1:26-28 completed. The dominion clause of Genesis 1:26 (reasserted from s40) returns, joined to the blessing of Genesis 1:28—be fruitful, multiply, replenish, subdue, have dominion. Psalm 8's fuller song of dominion is held for the closing prayer. Moses 2:26 (dominion, reasserted from s40) and Moses 2:28 give the first-person parallel; Abraham 4:26 (dominion, reasserted from s40) and Abraham 4:28 the account of the Gods, who 'will bless them' and cause them to multiply and subdue the earth.

b.text: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
b.comment: The dominion clause; reasserted from s40.

b.text: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
b.comment: The blessing: be fruitful, multiply, replenish, subdue, have dominion.

r.text: And I, God, said unto mine Only Begotten, which was with me from the beginning: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness; and it was so. And I, God, said: Let them have dominion over the fishes of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
r.comment: The dominion clause; reasserted from s40.

r.text: And I, God, blessed them, and said unto them: Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
r.comment: First-person parallel to the blessing.

r.text: And the Gods took counsel among themselves and said: Let us go down and form man in our image, after our likeness; and we will give them dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
r.comment: The dominion clause; reasserted from s40.

r.text: And the Gods said: We will bless them. And the Gods said: We will cause them to be fruitful and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it, and to have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
r.comment: The Gods 'will bless them' and cause them to multiply and subdue.

s48.tx: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them. And God looked upon everything that He had made.
s48.pc: The sixth day closes and the work is finished. Two clauses: 'the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them' (Genesis 2:1), and God's survey of all He had made (Genesis 1:31, whose 'very good' completes at s49). The three accounts converge: Moses 3:1 and Abraham 5:1 render the finishing (Abraham in the planning voice, 'thus we will finish'); Moses 2:31 and Abraham 4:31 render the survey—Abraham distinctively closing the day not with 'very good' but with 'they shall be very obedient,' the creation's answering submission to its Maker.

b.text: Thus the heavens and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
b.comment: The work finished, and all the host of them.

b.text: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
b.comment: God surveys all He had made; its 'very good' completes at s49.

r.text: Thus the heaven and the earth were finished, and all the host of them.
r.comment: First-person parallel to the finishing.

r.text: And I, God, saw everything that I had made, and, behold, all things which I had made were very good; and the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
r.comment: First-person survey; 'all things... were very good.' Carries s49.

r.text: And thus we will finish the heavens and the earth, and all the hosts of them.
r.comment: The Gods' planning voice: 'thus we will finish.'

r.text: And the Gods said: We will do everything that we have said, and organize them; and behold, they shall be very obedient. And it came to pass that it was from evening until morning they called night; and it came to pass that it was from morning until evening that they called day; and they numbered the sixth time.
r.comment: The Abraham account closes the sixth time distinctively: not 'very good' but 'very obedient.' Carries s49.

s49.tx: And behold, it was very good.
s49.pc: Genesis 1:31, its closing verdict—'behold, it was very good' (reasserted from s48). Moses 2:31 carries the same in first-person ('all things which I had made were very good'); Abraham 4:31 (reasserted from s48) renders the sixth-day close as 'very obedient,' the creation's submission standing where Genesis sets its goodness.

b.text: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
b.comment: 'Behold, it was very good'—the verdict on the whole; reasserted from s48.

r.text: And I, God, saw everything that I had made, and, behold, all things which I had made were very good; and the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
r.comment: 'All things which I had made were very good'; reasserted from s48.

r.text: And the Gods said: We will do everything that we have said, and organize them; and behold, they shall be very obedient. And it came to pass that it was from evening until morning they called night; and it came to pass that it was from morning until evening that they called day; and they numbered the sixth time.
r.comment: 'Very obedient'—the Abraham close; reasserted from s48.

s50.tx: The invisible God could be known through the visible creation.
s50.pc: A paraphrase of Romans 1:20—the invisible things of God clearly seen through the things that are made. The narration turns from the finished creation to what it reveals: the Creator known through His work. Job 12:7-9 gives the same in the sapiential voice, the beasts and the earth themselves teaching of God's hand. Restoration scripture presses it further: Alma 30:44, that the earth and its motion and the planets in their courses witness a Supreme Creator, and Moses 6:63, that all things bear record of Christ. Psalm 19's fuller song of the heavens' witness is kept for the closing prayer.

b.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:
b.comment: The invisible God clearly seen through the things that are made—the verse the narration compresses.

b.text: But ask now the beasts, and they shall teach thee; and the fowls of the air, and they shall tell thee: Or speak to the earth, and it shall teach thee: and the fishes of the sea shall declare unto thee. Who knoweth not in all these that the hand of the LORD hath wrought this?
b.comment: The creation itself teaching of God's hand.

r.text: …all things denote there is a God; yea, even the earth, and all things that are upon the face of it, yea, and its motion, yea, and also all the planets which move in their regular form do witness that there is a Supreme Creator.
r.comment: The earth, its motion, and the planets witness a Supreme Creator.

r.text: And behold, all things have their likeness, and all things are created and made to bear record of me, both things which are temporal, and things which are spiritual; things which are in the heavens above, and things which are on the earth, and things which are in the earth, and things which are under the earth, both above and beneath: all things bear record of me.
r.comment: All things made to bear record of Christ; anticipates the closing prayer's refrain.

s51.tx: Then God rested from all his work which He created and made.
s51.pc: Genesis 2:2-3—God rests on the seventh day, blesses it, and sanctifies it; the narration's 'which He created and made' is drawn from the verse's own close. Hebrews 4:4 sets the seventh-day rest in the New Testament's voice; Exodus 20:11 makes it the ground of the Sabbath command. Moses 3:2-3 gives the first-person parallel; Abraham 5:2-3 the account of the Gods, who rest 'on the seventh time.'

b.text: And on the seventh day God ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.
b.comment: God rests on the seventh day from all His work.

b.text: And God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it: because that in it he had rested from all his work which God created and made.
b.comment: The day blessed and sanctified; 'which God created and made'—the narration's close.

b.text: For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.
b.comment: The New Testament witness to the seventh-day rest.

b.text: For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it.
b.comment: The rest made the ground of the Sabbath command.

r.text: And on the seventh day I, God, ended my work, and all things which I had made; and I rested on the seventh day from all my work, and all things which I had made were finished, and I, God, saw that they were good;
r.comment: First-person parallel to the rest.

r.text: And I, God, blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it; because that in it I had rested from all my work which I, God, had created and made.
r.comment: The day blessed and sanctified, first person.

r.text: And the Gods said among themselves: On the seventh time we will end our work, which we have counseled; and we will rest on the seventh time from all our work which we have counseled.
r.comment: The Gods rest 'on the seventh time'—the Abraham distinctive.

r.text: And the Gods concluded upon the seventh time, because that on the seventh time they would rest from all their works which they (the Gods) counseled among themselves to form; and sanctified it. And thus were their decisions at the time that they counseled among themselves to form the heavens and the earth.
r.comment: The seventh-time rest concluded and sanctified.

s52.tx: God knew beforehand that Eden would not last, that humankind would be deceived, tempted, sin, and fall from the presence of God to mortality.
s52.pc: The Fall was foreseen, not a surprise. Before the garden, God knew its end from its beginning (Isaiah 46:9-10; Acts 15:18)—the death-warning of Genesis 2:17 was set with full knowledge of what would follow. Scripture holds God to be all-knowing (1 John 3:20; 2 Nephi 9:20; Moses 1:6), unable to be caught unaware (Hebrews 4:13), His purposes beyond thwarting (Job 42:2; Isaiah 14:27; Doctrine and Covenants 3:1). The Fall from God's presence and into mortality entered a plan already prepared, not a plan overturned.

b.text: Known unto God are all his works from the beginning of the world.
b.comment: Known unto God are all His works from the beginning.

b.text: Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure:
