b.comment: God declaring the end from the beginning; His counsel shall stand.

b.text: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
b.comment: The death-warning God set, knowing what would follow.

b.text: For if our heart condemn us, God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.
b.comment: God is greater than our heart, and knoweth all things.

b.text: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
b.comment: All things naked and opened unto His eyes—nothing hidden from Him.

b.text: I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee.
b.comment: He can do every thing; no thought can be withholden from Him.

b.text: For the LORD of hosts hath purposed, and who shall disannul it? and his hand is stretched out, and who shall turn it back?
b.comment: The LORD hath purposed; who shall disannul it?

b.text: Great is our Lord, and of great power: his understanding is infinite.
b.comment: His understanding is infinite.

r.text: O how great the holiness of our God! For he knoweth all things, and there is not anything save he knows it.
r.comment: He knoweth all things, and there is not anything save He knows it.

r.text: …there is no God beside me, and all things are present with me, for I know them all.
r.comment: All things present with Him; He knows them all.

r.text: The works, and the designs, and the purposes of God cannot be frustrated, neither can they come to naught.
r.comment: The purposes of God cannot be frustrated, neither come to naught.

s53.tx: Still, the father had chosen us in him before the foundation of the world.
s53.pc: Even foreseeing the Fall, the Father's choosing held. 'Chosen us in him before the foundation of the world' is Ephesians 1:4—reasserted from s2, where it grounds His foreknowledge of our existence; here it is election in Christ standing firm despite the foreseen Fall, the 'Still' of the narration. 2 Timothy 1:9 sets the same grace given in Christ before the world began. The Restoration adds Alma 13:3—called and prepared 'from the foundation of the world according to the foreknowledge of God.'

b.text: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:
b.comment: 'Chosen us in him before the foundation of the world'; reasserted from s2, here election standing despite the foreseen Fall.

b.text: Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given us in Christ Jesus before the world began,
b.comment: Grace given us in Christ Jesus before the world began.

b.text: Having predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,
b.comment: Predestinated unto adoption by Jesus Christ.

r.text: …being called and prepared from the foundation of the world according to the foreknowledge of God, on account of their exceeding faith and good works…
r.comment: Called and prepared from the foundation of the world according to the foreknowledge of God.

s54.tx: The dramatic events that took place in the garden led to the conditions of mortality and opposition in all things.
s54.pc: The Fall into mortality, and the opposition that came with it. By one man's transgression death entered the world (Romans 5:12; 1 Corinthians 15:21-22)—the fall into mortality all traditions affirm. The Restoration names the deeper pattern: 'opposition in all things' (2 Nephi 2:11), the compound of good and evil without which no choice could be made. Doctrine and Covenants 76:25-27 records the fall of the adversary himself—Lucifer, once in authority, thrust down—whose opposition works upon the garden and the world.

b.text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:
b.comment: By one man sin entered the world, and death by sin—the fall into mortality.

b.text: For since by man came death, by man came also the resurrection of the dead. For as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive.
b.comment: By man came death; in Adam all die.

r.text: For it must needs be, that there is an opposition in all things. If not so, my firstborn in the wilderness, righteousness could not be brought to pass, neither wickedness, neither holiness nor misery, neither good nor bad.
r.comment: The Restoration's naming of the pattern: opposition in all things.

r.text: And this we saw also, and bear record, that an angel of God who was in authority in the presence of God, who rebelled against the Only Begotten Son whom the Father loved and who was in the bosom of the Father, was thrust down from the presence of God and the Son, And was called Perdition, for the heavens wept over him—he was Lucifer, a son of the morning. And we beheld, and lo, he is fallen! is fallen, even a son of the morning!
r.comment: The adversary's own fall—Lucifer thrust down—the source of the opposition.

s55.tx: It was by God's plan that creation and the state of humankind was brought to their present state.
s55.pc: What the garden set in motion was not outside God's plan but within it. He 'worketh all things after the counsel of his own will' (Ephesians 1:11), toward 'the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus' (Ephesians 3:11), working all things together for good to His own (Romans 8:28). The Restoration bears the fullest witness: all was 'done in the wisdom of him who knoweth all things' (2 Nephi 2:24), for 'Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy' (2 Nephi 2:25, reasserted from s2b)—the Fall received into the great plan of happiness (Alma 42:8), for God 'bringeth about his great and eternal purposes, which were prepared from the foundation of the world' (Alma 42:26).

b.text: In whom also we have obtained an inheritance, being predestinated according to the purpose of him who worketh all things after the counsel of his own will:
b.comment: He worketh all things after the counsel of His own will.

b.text: According to the eternal purpose which he purposed in Christ Jesus our Lord:
b.comment: The eternal purpose which He purposed in Christ Jesus.

b.text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.
b.comment: All things work together for good, according to His purpose.

r.text: But behold, all things have been done in the wisdom of him who knoweth all things.
r.comment: All things done in the wisdom of Him who knoweth all things.

r.text: Adam fell that men might be; and men are, that they might have joy.
r.comment: Adam fell that men might be; men are, that they might have joy; reasserted from s2b.

r.text: Now behold, it was not expedient that man should be reclaimed from this temporal death, for that would destroy the great plan of happiness.
r.comment: The great plan of happiness, which the Fall serves rather than destroys.

r.text: And thus God bringeth about his great and eternal purposes, which were prepared from the foundation of the world.
r.comment: God brings about His great and eternal purposes, prepared from the foundation of the world.

s57.pc: The council seen at s17 is addressed again—now after the Fall. Scripture shows God amid a deliberating assembly: the host standing by His throne (1 Kings 22:19), God presiding in the congregation of the mighty (Psalm 82:1), the counsel of the LORD in which His word is heard and marked (Jeremiah 23:18). Restoration scripture names that same council—the noble and great ones organized before the world, God standing in the midst of them (Abraham 3:22-23), the Council of the Eternal God before this world was (Doctrine and Covenants 121:32). Reasserted from s17: there the council was convened before creation; here it is re-addressed as the remedy for the Fall is opened.

b.text: And he said, Hear thou therefore the word of the LORD: I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.
b.comment: The LORD enthroned amid all the host of heaven—the council seen; reasserted from s17.

b.text: God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.
b.comment: God presiding in the divine assembly; reasserted from s17.

b.text: For who hath stood in the counsel of the LORD, and hath perceived and heard his word? who hath marked his word, and heard it?
b.comment: The counsel of the LORD, His word heard and marked; reasserted from s17.

r.text: Now the Lord had shown unto me, Abraham, the intelligences that were organized before the world was; and among all these there were many of the noble and great ones; And God saw these souls that they were good, and he stood in the midst of them, and he said: These I will make my rulers; for he stood among those that were spirits, and he saw that they were good; and he said unto me: Abraham, thou art one of them; thou wast chosen before thou wast born.
r.comment: The noble and great ones organized before the world; God stood in the midst; reasserted from s17.

r.text: According to that which was ordained in the midst of the Council of the Eternal God of all other gods before this world was, that should be reserved unto the finishing and the end thereof, when every man shall enter into his eternal presence and into his immortal rest.
r.comment: Named plainly: the Council of the Eternal God, before this world was; reasserted from s17.

s58.tx: “Behold, mankind has become as one of us to know good and evil.”
s58.pc: Near-verbatim Genesis 3:22—'the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil.' The plural 'us' is the voice of the council just addressed. Moses 4:28 gives the Restoration parallel in the same words, spoken 'unto mine Only Begotten'—additional witness to that council voice, set beside the plain Genesis text.

b.text: And the LORD God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
b.comment: The words the narration renders: the man become as one of us.

r.text: And I, the Lord God, said unto mine Only Begotten: Behold, the man is become as one of us to know good and evil; and now lest he put forth his hand and partake also of the tree of life, and eat and live forever,
r.comment: The same words, spoken unto the Only Begotten—the council voice.

s59.tx: Then the Father asked, “Who shall I send?
s59.pc: Isaiah 6:8—'Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?' The Father's question, its 'us' again the voice of the council. The on-screen question stays in Isaiah's throne-room; the Restoration's answer to it—the Son's 'Here am I, send me'—is carried at s63, where the volunteering belongs.

b.text: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?
b.comment: The Father's question; its 'us' the voice of the council.

s60.tx: Who among you is willing to maintain the holy demands of justice while offering atoning mercy and divine grace?”
s60.pc: Who can satisfy justice and yet extend mercy? Scripture sets the two meeting in one place—'Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other' (Psalm 85:10)—and names the one in whom they are reconciled: God 'just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus' (Romans 3:26). The Restoration presses the same reconciliation: the atonement made 'to appease the demands of justice, that God might be a perfect, just God, and a merciful God also' (Alma 42:15), the last sacrifice bringing 'the bowels of mercy, which overpowereth justice,' so that 'mercy can satisfy the demands of justice' (Alma 34:15-16).

b.text: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
b.comment: Mercy and truth met; righteousness and peace kissed.

b.text: To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.
b.comment: God just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.

r.text: And now, the plan of mercy could not be brought about except an atonement should be made; therefore God himself atoneth for the sins of the world, to bring about the plan of mercy, to appease the demands of justice, that God might be a perfect, just God, and a merciful God also.
r.comment: The atonement to appease justice, that God be a just and a merciful God also.

r.text: …this being the intent of this last sacrifice, to bring about the bowels of mercy, which overpowereth justice… And thus mercy can satisfy the demands of justice, and encircles them in the arms of safety…
r.comment: The last sacrifice: the bowels of mercy overpowereth justice; mercy can satisfy its demands.

s61.tx: The Word saw that there was no one, and marveled that there was no intercessor.
s61.pc: The biblical hub of the beat: 'he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor' (Isaiah 59:16); the narration renders it 'no one... marveled.' The Restoration names who that intercessor would prove to be—the firstfruits who 'shall make intercession for all the children of men' (2 Nephi 2:9), the one 'standing betwixt them and justice,' having 'satisfied the demands of justice' (Mosiah 15:9). Isaiah 59:16 continues into s62.

b.text: And he saw that there was no man, and wondered that there was no intercessor…
b.comment: The hub: no man, no intercessor; its second clause carries to s62.

r.text: Wherefore, he is the firstfruits unto God, inasmuch as he shall make intercession for all the children of men; and they that believe in him shall be saved.
r.comment: The firstfruits who makes intercession for all the children of men.

r.text: …standing betwixt them and justice; having broken the bands of death, taken upon himself their iniquity and their transgressions, having redeemed them, and satisfied the demands of justice.
r.comment: Standing betwixt them and justice, having satisfied its demands—the intercessor named.

s62.tx: So by His own arm mankind must be saved.
s62.pc: Isaiah 59:16 completes here—'therefore his arm brought salvation'—reasserted from s61, its second clause now carried. Isaiah 63:5 doubles it: 'mine own arm brought salvation unto me.' If mankind is to be saved, it must be by His own arm—'neither is there salvation in any other' (Acts 4:12). The Restoration says the same: 'there shall be no other name given nor any other way nor means whereby salvation can come... only in and through the name of Christ' (Mosiah 3:17).

b.text: …therefore his arm brought salvation unto him; and his righteousness, it sustained him.
b.comment: His arm brought salvation; reasserted from s61.

b.text: And I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to uphold: therefore mine own arm brought salvation unto me; and my fury, it upheld me.
b.comment: Mine own arm brought salvation unto me—the arm doubled.

b.text: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
b.comment: Salvation in none other; no other name whereby we must be saved.

r.text: And moreover, I say unto you, that there shall be no other name given nor any other way nor means whereby salvation can come unto the children of men, only in and through the name of Christ, the Lord Omnipotent.
r.comment: No other name nor way whereby salvation can come, only in Christ.

s63.tx: He volunteered to be the Lamb, slain from the foundation of the world.
s63.pc: When no intercessor was found (s61), the Word Himself stepped forward. Scripture names Him the Lamb 'slain from the foundation of the world' (Revelation 13:8)—'the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world' (John 1:29), 'brought as a lamb to the slaughter' (Isaiah 53:7). The Restoration gives the volunteering in His own voice: to the Father's 'Whom shall I send?' the Beloved and Chosen from the beginning answered, 'Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever' (Moses 4:2); 'Here am I, send me' (Abraham 3:27, answering the question at s59).

b.text: …the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.
b.comment: The Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.

b.text: …Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
b.comment: Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.

b.text: …he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
b.comment: Brought as a lamb to the slaughter.

r.text: But, behold, my Beloved Son, which was my Beloved and Chosen from the beginning, said unto me—Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever.
r.comment: Christ's offer only—'Father, thy will be done'; the Beloved and Chosen from the beginning.

r.text: And the Lord said: Whom shall I send? And one answered like unto the Son of Man: Here am I, send me… And the Lord said: I will send the first.
r.comment: The Father's question answered—'Here am I, send me'; answering s59.

s64.tx: He was foreordained and anointed by God the Father before the foundation of the world, to be the Messiah who would show mankind the way and redeem souls unto the Father.
s64.pc: The One who volunteered was no afterthought: He was 'foreordained before the foundation of the world' (1 Peter 1:19-20). 'Messiah' means anointed—'the LORD hath anointed me' (Isaiah 61:1), 'God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power' (Acts 10:38), the LORD and 'his anointed' of the Psalms (Psalm 2:2). The Restoration reasserts the foreordination: the Beloved 'Chosen from the beginning' (Moses 4:2, reasserted from s63), the atonement 'prepared from the foundation of the world' (Mosiah 4:6-7), 'he who was prepared from the foundation of the world to redeem my people' (Ether 3:14), a calling 'prepared from the foundation of the world according to the foreknowledge of God' (Alma 13:3, reasserted from s53).

b.text: …as of a lamb without blemish and without spot: Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you,
b.comment: Foreordained before the foundation of the world.

b.text: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek…
b.comment: The LORD hath anointed me.

b.text: …God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power…
b.comment: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power.

b.text: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the LORD, and against his anointed…
b.comment: The LORD and his anointed—the Messiah.

r.text: But, behold, my Beloved Son, which was my Beloved and Chosen from the beginning, said unto me—Father, thy will be done, and the glory be thine forever.
r.comment: Chosen from the beginning; reasserted from s63.

r.text: …the atonement which has been prepared from the foundation of the world, that thereby salvation might come to him that should put his trust in the Lord…
r.comment: The atonement prepared from the foundation of the world.

r.text: Behold, I am he who was prepared from the foundation of the world to redeem my people. Behold, I am Jesus Christ. I am the Father and the Son…
r.comment: He who was prepared from the foundation of the world to redeem His people.

r.text: …being called and prepared from the foundation of the world according to the foreknowledge of God, on account of their exceeding faith and good works…
r.comment: Called and prepared from the foundation of the world according to God's foreknowledge; reasserted from s53.

s65.tx: The Word who created heaven and earth, Jehovah of the Old Testament, was the same God that would be born as Jesus of Nazareth, the Savior and Redeemer of the world.
s65.pc: The film's climax names Him plainly: the Word who made heaven and earth, the Jehovah of the Old Testament, is Jesus of Nazareth. The identity turns on one name—'I AM.' God named Himself to Moses 'I AM THAT I AM' (Exodus 3:14); Jesus took that name to Himself: 'Before Abraham was, I am' (John 8:58). He is 'the first, and… the last; and beside me there is no God' (Isaiah 44:6), 'the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour' (Isaiah 43:11), 'he that liveth, and was dead' (Revelation 1:17-18). The Restoration confirms the same identity: 'I am he that gave the law… I am he who covenanted with my people Israel' (3 Nephi 15:5); the voice of Jehovah, 'I am he who was slain; I am your advocate with the Father' (Doctrine and Covenants 110:3-4); 'the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and the God of Jacob' who 'yieldeth himself… to be crucified' (1 Nephi 19:10); 'My name is Jehovah' (Abraham 2:8); 'even Jesus Christ, the Great I Am' (Doctrine and Covenants 38:1, reasserted from s17).

b.text: And God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM…
b.comment: God names Himself: I AM THAT I AM.

b.text: Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.
b.comment: Jesus takes the I AM to Himself: before Abraham was, I am.

b.text: Thus saith the LORD the King of Israel, and his redeemer the LORD of hosts; I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God.
b.comment: The LORD, the first and the last, beside whom no God.

b.text: I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour.
b.comment: The LORD, beside whom there is no saviour.

b.text: …Fear not; I am the first and the last: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen…
b.comment: The first and the last; he that liveth, and was dead.

r.text: Behold, I am he that gave the law, and I am he who covenanted with my people Israel; therefore, the law in me is fulfilled…
r.comment: I am he that gave the law and covenanted with Israel.

r.text: …even the voice of Jehovah, saying: I am the first and the last; I am he who liveth, I am he who was slain; I am your advocate with the Father.
r.comment: The voice of Jehovah—slain, and advocate with the Father.

r.text: …the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, yieldeth himself, according to the words of the angel, as a man, into the hands of wicked men, to be lifted up… and to be crucified…
r.comment: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, yielded to be crucified.

r.text: My name is Jehovah, and I know the end from the beginning; therefore my hand shall be over thee.
r.comment: My name is Jehovah.

r.text: Thus saith the Lord your God, even Jesus Christ, the Great I Am, Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end…
r.comment: Jesus Christ, the Great I Am; reasserted from s17 (there the pre-creation beholding, here the I AM naming).

s66.tx: Before withdrawing His presence from the children He had created, God made coats of skins of animals to clothe them.
s66.pc: The last mercy in the garden: God Himself clothes them. Before they are sent away, the Lord God makes coats of skins and clothes the man and his wife (Genesis 3:21); Moses 4:27 gives the same in first-person voice. The narration's 'before withdrawing His presence' looks ahead to the expulsion at s67—the new act here is the covering. Scripture elsewhere makes a God-given garment a figure of His covering, the garments of salvation and the robe of righteousness (Isaiah 61:10); the resonance is offered, not pressed. The plain wonder stands first: the Maker stoops to clothe the creatures He made.

b.text: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the LORD God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
b.comment: God Himself makes coats of skins and clothes them—the last act before the sending-forth.

b.text: …he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of righteousness…
b.comment: A God-given garment as a figure of His covering—garments of salvation, robe of righteousness; offered as resonance, not pressed.

r.text: Unto Adam, and also unto his wife, did I, the Lord God, make coats of skins, and clothed them.
r.comment: The same clothing in first-person Restoration voice.

s67.tx: He gave them instructions and sent them forth from Eden to till the ground from whence mankind was taken.
s67.pc: The expulsion. The Lord God sends the man forth from Eden to till the ground from whence he was taken (Genesis 3:23); Moses 4:29 gives the first-person parallel. The narration does not name the cherubim, but the beat closes in Genesis with the flaming sword set to keep the way of the tree of life (Genesis 3:24; Moses 4:31)—the guarding that makes the loss of Eden real, offered here as additional witness though the film's text passes over it. That same way to the tree of life is the promise restored at s81.

b.text: Therefore the LORD God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.
b.comment: Sent forth from Eden to till the ground from whence he was taken—the words the narration renders.

b.text: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
b.comment: The expulsion completed: the flaming sword set to keep the way of the tree of life; not named on-screen, offered as the beat's close.

r.text: Therefore I, the Lord God, will send him forth from the Garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken;
r.comment: The sending-forth in first-person Restoration voice.

r.text: So I drove out the man, and I placed at the east of the Garden of Eden, cherubim and a flaming sword, which turned every way to keep the way of the tree of life.
r.comment: Cherubim and a flaming sword—the guarding of the tree of life whose way is restored at s81.

s68.tx: The Word came to Adam, “In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground.
s68.pc: Genesis 3:19, its first clause—the sentence of labor unto death. Genesis 3:19 carries s68 through s70, split at its clauses (the one-verse-split pattern of s9-s11 and s41-s42). Moses 4:25 gives the Restoration parallel across all three clauses, with two distinctives: it folds the death-warning into the sentence—'for thou shalt surely die'—and reads 'dust thou wast' where the King James reads 'dust thou art.'

b.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
b.comment: 'In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground'—the first clause; the verse continues through s70.

r.text: By the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, until thou shalt return unto the ground—for thou shalt surely die—for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou wast, and unto dust shalt thou return.
r.comment: The Restoration parallel, carrying s68 through s70; it folds in the death-warning and reads 'dust thou wast.'

s69.tx: For out of it was thou taken.
s69.pc: Genesis 3:19, its middle clause—'for out of it wast thou taken'—reasserted from s68: man returns to the ground he was drawn from. Moses 4:25 (reasserted from s68) carries the same.

b.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
b.comment: 'For out of it wast thou taken'—the middle clause; reasserted from s68.

r.text: By the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, until thou shalt return unto the ground—for thou shalt surely die—for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou wast, and unto dust shalt thou return.
r.comment: The same, in the Restoration sentence; reasserted from s68.

s70.tx: For dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.”
s70.pc: Genesis 3:19, its final clause—'for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return' (reasserted from s68), the plainest naming of mortality. The Wisdom books take it up: all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again (Ecclesiastes 3:20); He remembereth that we are dust (Psalm 103:14)—the mercy folded into the naming. Moses 4:25 (reasserted from s68) closes the same way, reading 'dust thou wast.'

b.text: In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.
b.comment: 'For dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return'—the final clause; reasserted from s68.

b.text: All go unto one place; all are of the dust, and all turn to dust again.
b.comment: 'All are of the dust, and all turn to dust again'—the same mortality in the Wisdom voice.

b.text: For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.
b.comment: 'He remembereth that we are dust'—the mercy folded into the naming.

r.text: By the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, until thou shalt return unto the ground—for thou shalt surely die—for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou wast, and unto dust shalt thou return.
r.comment: The Restoration close, 'dust thou wast'; reasserted from s68.

s71.tx: Most important of all these events, God promised eventual victory over evil and the fall of mankind.
s71.pc: The first promise of the gospel—the protoevangelium. In the same breath that curses the serpent, God sets enmity between it and the woman and promises a seed who will bruise its head (Genesis 3:15); the Restoration gives the same in first-person voice (Moses 4:21). The New Testament names the victory that promise carried: the God of peace bruising Satan under our feet (Romans 16:20), the Son of God manifested to destroy the works of the devil (1 John 3:8), who took flesh and blood that through death He might destroy him that had the power of death (Hebrews 2:14). The narration's 'most important' is well judged—what is spoken over the fallen pair is not the curse but the promise folded inside it.

b.text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
b.comment: The protoevangelium—the seed of the woman to bruise the serpent's head.

b.text: And the God of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly…
b.comment: The promise carried to its end: the God of peace bruising Satan underfoot.

b.text: …For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.
b.comment: The Son of God manifested to destroy the works of the devil.

b.text: Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
b.comment: Through death He destroys him that had the power of death—victory over the Fall's own sting.

r.text: And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, between thy seed and her seed; and he shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.
r.comment: The same promise in first-person Restoration voice.

s72.tx: Adam was comforted by the promise of eternal life God made from before the world began, knowing God cannot lie.
s72.pc: The comfort rests on two things—the promise and the Promiser. Titus 1:2 gives both in one line: eternal life, which God that cannot lie promised before the world began. Hebrews 6:18 makes God's truthfulness the ground of a strong consolation; Numbers 23:19 states it plainly—God is not a man, that He should lie. The Restoration bears the same witness in Ether 3:12 (a God of truth, and canst not lie) and Enos 1:6, where knowing God could not lie is what sweeps guilt away. And it shows Adam himself comforted: blessing God and prophesying that in this life he should have joy, and again in the flesh see God (Moses 5:10).

b.text: In hope of eternal life, which God, that cannot lie, promised before the world began;
b.comment: Both at once: eternal life, and the God that cannot lie who promised it before the world began.

b.text: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
b.comment: God's truthfulness made the ground of a strong consolation—the comfort itself.

b.text: God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
b.comment: 'God is not a man, that he should lie'—the plainest form of the comfort.

r.text: And he answered: Yea, Lord, I know that thou speakest the truth, for thou art a God of truth, and canst not lie.
r.comment: A God of truth, and canst not lie.

r.text: And I, Enos, knew that God could not lie; wherefore, my guilt was swept away.
r.comment: Knowing God could not lie is what sweeps guilt away—the comfort enacted.

r.text: And in that day Adam blessed God and was filled, and began to prophesy concerning all the families of the earth, saying: Blessed be the name of God, for because of my transgression my eyes are opened, and in this life I shall have joy, and again in the flesh I shall see God.
r.comment: Adam himself comforted: he blesses God and prophesies joy in this life, and to see God again in the flesh.

s73.tx: By Divine Will we experience desire, hardship, sorrow, temptations, enmity, labor, and death.
s73.pc: The conditions of mortal life, ordered rather than accidental. Genesis names them at the Fall: sorrow and desire for the woman (Genesis 3:16), the cursed ground and lifelong toil for the man (Genesis 3:17)—the death already carried at s68-s70. Paul sets them within God's will: the creation subjected to vanity 'not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope,' groaning and travailing until now (Romans 8:20-22). The Restoration gathers the whole inheritance into one line—'by his fall came death; and we are made partakers of misery and woe' (Moses 6:48). The narration's 'Divine Will' is Paul's 'in hope': the hardship is permitted toward an end.

b.text: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.
b.comment: Sorrow and desire—the conditions spoken to the woman.

b.text: …cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;
b.comment: The cursed ground and lifelong toil—spoken to the man.

b.text: For the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who hath subjected the same in hope… For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.
b.comment: The conditions set within God's will—subjected in hope, the creation groaning until now.

r.text: And he said unto them: Because that Adam fell, we are; and by his fall came death; and we are made partakers of misery and woe.
r.comment: The whole inheritance named: by the fall, death and 'misery and woe.'

s74.tx: But this is not all we were also meant to know fulfillment, comfort, joy, holy inspiration, love, rest, and life. For each of these life experiences carries its opposite that we might know the one by the other.
s74.pc: The principle beneath the pairing—we know by contrast. Ecclesiastes states it as God's own ordering: 'God also hath set the one over against the other' (Ecclesiastes 7:14), and lays out the paired times, to weep and to laugh, to mourn and to dance (Ecclesiastes 3:1-8). The Restoration names it 'opposition in all things' (2 Nephi 2:11, reasserted from s54)—there the opposition enters with the Fall; here it is the epistemic principle: without misery no joy, without sin no good (2 Nephi 2:23), for 'if they never should have bitter they could not know the sweet' (Doctrine and Covenants 29:39). Not a fortunate fall pressed on the reader—only the plain claim that the opposites teach each other.

b.text: In the day of prosperity be joyful, but in the day of adversity consider: God also hath set the one over against the other…
b.comment: 'God also hath set the one over against the other'—the pairing as God's own ordering.

b.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:… a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to mourn, and a time to dance;
b.comment: The paired times—to weep and to laugh, to mourn and to dance.

r.text: For it must needs be, that there is an opposition in all things. If not so, my firstborn in the wilderness, righteousness could not be brought to pass, neither wickedness, neither holiness nor misery, neither good nor bad.
r.comment: 'Opposition in all things'; reasserted from s54—there entering with the Fall, here the principle of knowing by contrast.

r.text: And they would have had no children; wherefore they would have remained in a state of innocence, having no joy, for they knew no misery; doing no good, for they knew no sin.
r.comment: Without misery, no joy; without sin, no good.

r.text: And it must needs be that the devil should tempt the children of men, or they could not be agents unto themselves; for if they never should have bitter they could not know the sweet—
r.comment: 'If they never should have bitter they could not know the sweet.'

s75.tx: Adam taught his posterity of God's promises of salvation from evil, and redemption from the fall from God's presence.
s75.pc: The promise did not stop with Adam; it was handed down. Scripture makes the teaching of the generations a sacred charge—the fathers to make God's works known to the children, and they to theirs (Psalm 78:4-6), taking heed lest they forget, teaching them 'thy sons, and thy sons' sons' (Deuteronomy 4:9). The Restoration supplies the scene the Bible leaves implicit at Eden's edge: Adam and Eve 'made all things known unto their sons and their daughters' (Moses 5:12), under commandment to 'teach these things freely unto your children' (Moses 6:58)—the promise of redemption from the Fall passed hand to hand from the first parents.

b.text: We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD … That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children:
b.comment: The charge to declare God's works to the generation to come.

b.text: …but teach them thy sons, and thy sons’ sons;
b.comment: The generations taught, lest the things seen be forgotten.

r.text: And Adam and Eve blessed the name of God, and they made all things known unto their sons and their daughters.
r.comment: The direct witness: the first parents make all things known to their children.

r.text: Therefore I give unto you a commandment, to teach these things freely unto your children…
r.comment: The teaching made a divine commandment.

s76.tx: From that time, men began to call upon the name of the Lord.
s76.pc: Genesis 4:26 in the narration's own words—'then began men to call upon the name of the LORD,' spoken of the generation of Enos, Seth's son. The Restoration carries the same beginning: Adam and Eve 'called upon the name of the Lord' at the veil of Eden (Moses 5:4), and in the days of Seth and Enos 'began these men to call upon the name of the Lord, and the Lord blessed them' (Moses 6:4)—the worship of the first families taking its settled form.

b.text: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the LORD.
b.comment: The verse the narration renders.

r.text: And Adam and Eve, his wife, called upon the name of the Lord, and they heard the voice of the Lord from the way toward the Garden of Eden, speaking unto them, and they saw him not; for they were shut out from his presence.
r.comment: The first parents calling on the Lord at Eden's edge.

r.text: And then began these men to call upon the name of the Lord, and the Lord blessed them;
r.comment: The Restoration parallel to Genesis 4:26, in the line of Seth.

s77.tx: Their faith and hope were expressed through prayer, worship, and through sacrifices that foreshadowed the atoning sacrifice of the promised Messiah.
s77.pc: Faith took three forms—prayer, worship, and sacrifice—and the sacrifice was a shadow cast forward. Abel's was the first, offered 'by faith' and still speaking (Hebrews 11:4); the law that followed had only 'a shadow of good things to come' (Hebrews 10:1), for 'Christ our passover is sacrificed for us' (1 Corinthians 5:7). The Restoration names the shadow's meaning outright: Adam offered the firstlings 'for an offering unto the Lord' (Moses 5:5), and the angel told him why—'This thing is a similitude of the sacrifice of the Only Begotten of the Father' (Moses 5:7); the whole law was 'every whit pointing to that great and last sacrifice... the Son of God' (Alma 34:14, whose neighbor verses stand at s60 on mercy and justice). The biblical witness carries the foreshadowing on its own; the Restoration makes the type explicit.

b.text: By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, God testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.
b.comment: The first post-Fall sacrifice, offered by faith.

b.text: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
b.comment: Sacrifice as shadow of the good things to come.

b.text: …For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us:
b.comment: The paschal type named: Christ our passover.

r.text: And he gave unto them commandments, that they should worship the Lord their God, and should offer the firstlings of their flocks, for an offering unto the Lord. And Adam was obedient unto the commandments of the Lord.
r.comment: Worship and the offering of the firstlings commanded.

r.text: And then the angel spake, saying: This thing is a similitude of the sacrifice of the Only Begotten of the Father, which is full of grace and truth.
r.comment: The sacrifice named a similitude of the Only Begotten.

r.text: And behold, this is the whole meaning of the law, every whit pointing to that great and last sacrifice; and that great and last sacrifice will be the Son of God, yea, infinite and eternal.
r.comment: The whole law pointing to the great and last sacrifice, the Son of God.

s78.tx: The Great Patriarchs and Prophets knew these things since the world began.
s78.pc: The knowledge was not new with the patriarchs; it reached back to the beginning. God spoke 'by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began' (Luke 1:70; Acts 3:21), and those prophets 'died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off' (Hebrews 11:13). The Restoration says the same in the first person of the record-keepers: 'we knew of Christ, and we had a hope of his glory many hundred years before his coming; and not only we ourselves... but also all the holy prophets which were before us' (Jacob 4:4), for 'all the prophets who have prophesied ever since the world began' spoke of the coming Messiah (Mosiah 13:33). What the prophets knew is here; how the Spirit of Christ testified it in them is carried at s80.

b.text: As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began:
b.comment: The holy prophets since the world began.

b.text: Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began.
b.comment: All His holy prophets since the world began.

b.text: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.
b.comment: The patriarchs saw the promises afar off and died in faith.

r.text: For, for this intent have we written these things, that they may know that we knew of Christ, and we had a hope of his glory many hundred years before his coming; and not only we ourselves had a hope of his glory, but also all the holy prophets which were before us.
r.comment: All the holy prophets before them had hope of Christ's glory.

r.text: For behold, did not Moses prophesy unto them concerning the coming of the Messiah, and that God should redeem his people? Yea, and even all the prophets who have prophesied ever since the world began—have they not spoken more or less concerning these things?
r.comment: All the prophets since the world began spoke of the Messiah.

s79.tx: Each of them learning to walk with God.
s79.pc: 'Walk with God' is the Bible's own phrase for the life of the faithful patriarchs—Enoch, who 'walked with God: and he was not; for God took him' (Genesis 5:22-24), and Noah, 'a just man and perfect in his generations,' who 'walked with God' (Genesis 6:9); Micah gathers the charge for all, 'to walk humbly with thy God' (Micah 6:8). The Restoration keeps the same words: to Enoch the Lord said 'walk with me' (Moses 6:34); Noah 'walked with God, as did also his three sons' (Moses 8:27); and 'Enoch and all his people walked with God' until Zion was received up (Moses 7:69)—each of them, and a whole city, learning the one walk.

b.text: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years … And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.
b.comment: Enoch, who walked with God and was taken.

b.text: These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.
b.comment: Noah, who walked with God.

b.text: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
b.comment: The charge for all: to walk humbly with thy God.

r.text: Behold my Spirit is upon you, wherefore all thy words will I justify; and the mountains shall flee before you, and the rivers shall turn from their course; and thou shalt abide in me, and I in you; therefore walk with me.
r.comment: The Lord's word to Enoch: walk with me.

r.text: And thus Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord; for Noah was a just man, and perfect in his generation; and he walked with God, as did also his three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
r.comment: Noah and his sons walked with God (the Restoration extends it to the sons).

r.text: And Enoch and all his people walked with God, and he dwelt in the midst of Zion; and it came to pass that Zion was not, for God received it up into his own bosom; and from thence went forth the saying, Zion is Fled.
r.comment: A whole people—Zion—walked with God.

s80.tx: For the Spirit of Christ, which was in them, testified before hand of the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow those that do His commandments.
s80.pc: 1 Peter 1:11 in the narration's own words—'the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.' What the prophets carried (s78) was this: not general foresight but the Spirit of Christ Himself bearing witness of His sufferings and glory. Revelation names the principle—'the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy' (Revelation 19:10). The Restoration shows it enacted: to Sherem, Jacob declared that 'none of the prophets have written, nor prophesied, save they have spoken concerning this Christ' (Jacob 7:11); and Enoch, seeing the day of the Son of Man, watched 'the Lamb... slain from the foundation of the world' and rejoiced (Moses 7:47)—the sufferings and the glory beheld beforehand.

b.text: Searching what, or what manner of time the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify, when it testified beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow.
b.comment: The verse the narration renders: the Spirit of Christ testifying beforehand.

b.text: …worship God: for the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.
b.comment: The prophetic Spirit is the testimony of Jesus.

r.text: …none of the prophets have written, nor prophesied, save they have spoken concerning this Christ.
r.comment: Every prophet spoke concerning Christ.

r.text: And behold, Enoch saw the day of the coming of the Son of Man, even in the flesh; and his soul rejoiced, saying: The Righteous is lifted up, and the Lamb is slain from the foundation of the world; and through faith I am in the bosom of the Father, and behold, Zion is with me.
r.comment: Enoch beholds the sufferings and the glory beforehand.

s81.tx: For they will have the right to the Tree of Life restored to them as they enter through the gates into the Kingdom of Heaven.
s81.pc: The beat that began with the flaming sword closes with the gate. At s67 the way to the tree of life was guarded and Eden lost; here the right to that tree is restored to the faithful, who 'enter in through the gates' (Revelation 22:14; Revelation 2:7, 'to him that overcometh... the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God'). The Restoration gives the restored access in Christ's own invitation—'Come unto me and ye shall partake of the fruit of the tree of life' (Alma 5:34)—and names the gate and its keeper: 'the keeper of the gate is the Holy One of Israel... and there is none other way save it be by the gate' (2 Nephi 9:41). The tree itself is 'the greatest of all the gifts of God' (1 Nephi 15:36). What the Fall closed, the promised Messiah opens.

b.text: Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city.
b.comment: Right to the tree of life, and entrance through the gates—the hub.

b.text: …To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.
b.comment: The overcomer given the tree of life in the paradise of God.

r.text: Yea, he saith: Come unto me and ye shall partake of the fruit of the tree of life; yea, ye shall eat and drink of the bread and the waters of life freely;
r.comment: Christ's own invitation to partake of the tree of life.

r.text: …the way for man is narrow, but it lieth in a straight course before him, and the keeper of the gate is the Holy One of Israel; and he employeth no servant there; and there is none other way save it be by the gate; for he cannot be deceived, for the Lord God is his name.
r.comment: The gate, and its keeper the Holy One of Israel.

r.text: Wherefore, the wicked are rejected from the righteous, and also from that tree of life, whose fruit is most precious and most desirable above all other fruits; yea, and it is the greatest of all the gifts of God.
r.comment: The tree of life, the greatest of all the gifts of God.

s83.tx: We lift our eyes to the work of your fingers.

s84.tx: The moon and the stars you set in their places.

s85.tx: And the heavens declare your glory.

s86.tx: The skies proclaim the work of your hands.

s87.tx: Day after day they shout their witness.

s88.tx: Night after night they reveal knowledge.

s91.tx: Their voice still carries to the ends of the earth.

s92.tx: And so we come before You and wonder...

s93.tx: Through your Beloved Son, You made all this, and us.

s94.tx: You are the Divine Shepherd of the starry host, calling each of them by name and by Your great power, Not one of them is missing.

s95.tx: By Your word the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of Your mouth.

s96.tx: When You laid the foundations, the Morning Stars sang together, and the Children of God shouted for joy.

s97.tx: All things bear witness of You. The earth and everything upon it.

s98.tx: Its motion and the planets moving in their fixed courses.

s99.tx: The earth turns upon her wings.

s100.tx: The sun gives light by day, the moon by night.

s101.tx: And the stars shine as they move in their glory.

s102.tx: And in even the least of these, we have seen You moving in majesty and power.

s103.tx: We thank You that nothing You have made is without its witness.

s104.tx: The animals teach us of You.

s105.tx: The birds of the sky tell of You.

s106.tx: The earth instructs us, and the fish of the sea declare the work of Your hand.

s107.tx: For which of them does not know that Your hand has done this?

s108.tx: All things You have made bear witness of You.

s109.tx: Things in the heavens above, things upon the earth, things beneath. All of them testify of You.

s110.tx: Everything You have given points to You.

s111.tx: And in the fullness of it all we behold Your Son, through whom all things were made.

s112.tx: He came to us as an offering, a sacrifice to save and redeem the world.

s113.tx: And into all this vastness, You still turn Your face toward us.

s114.tx: What are we that You keep us in mind?

s115.tx: What are mortal children that You care for us?

s116.tx: Yet You have made us a little lower than the angels, and crowned us with glory and honor.

s117.tx: You have given us charge over the works of Your hands and entrusted the earth to our care.

s118.tx: You created us in Your own image and called us Your own.

s119.tx: For this we have no worthy words, only thanks.

s121.tx: Oh, Father, let us never fail to see it.

s122.tx: Since the world was made, Your unseen qualities, Your eternal power, Your very nature have been plain in the things You have made.

s123.tx: And we will not turn our eyes away.

s124.tx: So we confess Your hand in all things, and withhold nothing from Your will.

s125.tx: All creation answers You, and we answer with it.

s126.tx: Let the sun and moon praise You.

s127.tx: Let all the shining stars praise You.

s129.tx: For at Your command they were created.

s130.tx: The hills break forth and singing before You.

s131.tx: And all the trees of the field clap their hands for joy.

s132.tx: God our Father, how majestic is Your name in all the earth.

s133.tx: Send us from this place with eyes open to Your glory, hearts humbled by Your goodness, and hands willing to care for all You have made.

s134.tx: We offer this prayer in the name of Your Son, Jesus Christ.
